title: Florida's 5th Congressional District 2026 Election
description: The 2026 election for Florida's 5th Congressional District will be decided in the August 18 primary and November 3 general election. Incumbent Republican John Rutherford, a former Jacksonville Sheriff first elected in 2016, is seeking a fifth term and faces a primary challenge from conservative radio host and podcaster Mark Kaye. On the Democratic side, biomedical engineer Rachel Grage and project management professional Mark Heggestad are competing in the primary. The district covers portions of Duval and St. Johns Counties in Northeast Florida and is rated as Solid/Safe Republican by nonpartisan election forecasters. The race takes place under a new congressional map enacted in 2026 that is expected to maintain a strong Republican advantage.

candidates.name: John Rutherford
candidates.summary: John Rutherford is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Florida's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2016. He previously served as Jacksonville Sheriff for 12 years and spent 41 years with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office. In Congress, he sits on the House Appropriations Committee and has focused on law enforcement, military, and appropriations issues.

candidates.name: Rachel Grage
candidates.summary: Rachel Grage is a biomedical engineer and grassroots activist running for Congress in Florida's 5th District. She holds bachelor's and master's degrees in engineering from Tulane University and has worked on biomedical research including cardiac interventions and therapies for children with cerebral palsy. Her campaign focuses on affordability, healthcare access, accountability in government, and protecting Medicare and Social Security.

candidates.summary: Mark Heggestad is a certified Project Management Professional (PMP) and longtime football official running for Congress as a pragmatic Democrat focused on bipartisanship. His campaign emphasizes lowering political tensions, protecting democracy, and creating economic opportunities for working families in Northeast Florida.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available for this race, which tempers confidence. However, the race fundamentals overwhelmingly favor Republicans: the district is consistently rated as Solid/Safe Republican by nonpartisan forecasters, the new 2026 congressional map is expected to preserve a strong Republican advantage, and incumbent John Rutherford is a well-established four-term officeholder and former Jacksonville Sheriff who has dominated fundraising (over $500K raised). The Republican primary challenge from conservative radio host Mark Kaye introduces some nomination uncertainty, but both Republican contenders would be heavily favored in this Republican-leaning district covering portions of Duval and St. Johns Counties. The Democratic primary features two first-time candidates (Rachel Grage and Mark Heggestad) with no elected office experience. Given the structural stronghold and incumbency, a Republican general-election victory remains near-certain, justifying a safe_r rating with 96% projected Republican win probability and an estimated margin of roughly 22 points, consistent with recent district performance.
